title: assert
summary: Throw an error when a condition is false, matching MATLAB and RunMat assert semantics.

gpu_support.notes: The documented gpuArray form executes on the client. Conditions and scalar formatting replacements gather through authoritative typed storage before host evaluation; all eight integer classes remain exact.

description: `assert(cond, ...)` throws when a logical or logically convertible condition is false and has no public output. A real numeric condition is true only when it is nonempty and every element is nonzero; NaN cannot convert to logical. Optional text supplies a formatted message and a qualified error identifier.
behaviors: The documented condition is logical or convertible to logical. Logical, character, and real numeric conditions pass only when nonempty and every element is nonzero. All eight integer classes are tested directly from authoritative storage. NaN cannot convert to logical, and complex conditions are a mode-gated RunMat extension.
`assert(cond)` raises `RunMat:assertion:failed` with message `Assertion failed.` when `cond` is false.

`assert(cond, msg, A...)` formats `msg` with `sprintf`-compatible conversions. Each documented A is a character vector, string scalar, or numeric scalar; integer scalar values remain exact through decimal, unsigned, hexadecimal, and string formatting.

`assert(cond, errID, msg, A...)` requires colon-separated identifier fields that each begin with a letter and otherwise contain letters, digits, or underscores. Automatic `RunMat:` qualification of an unqualified identifier is a mode-gated RunMat extension.

Arguments are validated strictly: identifiers and message templates must be string scalars or character vectors, replacement arrays reject, and malformed format strings raise `RunMat:assertion:invalidInput`.
The public gpuArray form executes on the client. Resident conditions and scalar numeric replacements gather through typed storage; no assertion kernel runs on the GPU.

examples.description: Checking that all elements are nonzero
Attaching a custom identifier for tooling
Guarding GPU computations without manual gathering
examples.input:
G = gpuArray(rand(1024, 1));
assert(all(G > 0), "All entries must be positive.")

examples.description: Converting NaN checks into assertion failures
Ensuring structure fields exist before use
examples.input:
cfg = struct("timeout", 30, "rate", 60);
assert(isfield(cfg, "rate"), ...
       "runmat:config:missingField", ...
       "Configuration missing required field '%s'.", "rate")

faqs.question: What types can I pass as the condition?
faqs.answer: Logical arrays, character arrays, and real numeric arrays are accepted when convertible to a logical condition. Strings, cells, structs, and other unsupported values reject. Complex conditions are available only in RunMat compatibility mode.

faqs.question: How are NaN values treated?
faqs.answer: NaN cannot be converted to logical, so a real condition containing NaN raises the invalid-condition diagnostic rather than an ordinary assertion failure.

faqs.question: Do empty arrays pass the assertion?
faqs.answer: No. A condition is true only when its result is nonempty and all elements are nonzero, so empty logical, character, or real numeric conditions fail the assertion.

faqs.question: Can I omit the namespace in the message identifier?
faqs.answer: Only in RunMat compatibility mode. The documented form requires colon-separated component and mnemonic fields; RunMat mode can prefix an unqualified identifier with `RunMat:`.

faqs.question: What happens if my format string is malformed?
faqs.answer: The builtin raises `RunMat:assertion:invalidInput` describing the formatting issue.

faqs.question: Does `assert` run on the GPU?
faqs.answer: No. GPU tensors are gathered automatically and evaluated on the CPU to preserve MATLAB semantics.

faqs.question: Can I use strings for messages and identifiers?
faqs.answer: Yes. Both character vectors and string scalars are accepted for identifiers and message templates.

faqs.question: What value does `assert` return when the condition is true?
faqs.answer: `assert` has no public output. RunMat uses an internal control-flow sentinel only to complete runtime dispatch.

faqs.question: How do I disable assertions in production code?
faqs.answer: Wrap the condition in an `if` statement controlled by your own flag; MATLAB (and RunMat) always evaluates `assert`.

faqs.question: How do I distinguish assertion failures from other errors?
faqs.answer: Provide a custom identifier (for example `runmat:module:assertFailed`) and catch it in a `try`/`catch` block.

gpu_behavior: `assert` is a control-flow builtin. Public documentation accepts gpuArray input but states that execution does not run on the GPU. RunMat therefore gathers resident logical, real numeric, and scalar formatting values through authoritative typed storage before host evaluation; all eight integer classes remain exact, and no provider assertion kernel is launched.
